thesis: Every input today sells the layer that says what an agent may do, while Shadow already holds the rarer thing, a recorded 20/20 true-close audit whose own continue condition (zero false closes over twenty-plus closures authorizes widening auto-close by one commitment class) has not been acted on, so the frontier is not another authorization or orchestration comparison but converting a verified outcome into a delegation expansion; the commercial hypothesis that a buyer prices a governed function by its stated false-close rate before its harness stays deferred until Shadow itself has expanded responsibility on that rate and observed whether Will's review burden actually fell.
doctrine: When a bounded test finishes and its pre-declared continue condition is met, executing that condition outranks any new research synthesis; a loop that records verdicts but never spends them is verification theater.
proof_artifact: One commitment class moved from Will-reviewed close to Shadow auto-close, with the change citing the shipped false-close audit as its authorization receipt, a pre-declared revert condition (any false close or stale resurface in that class during the next review cycle reverts it), and tests passing before push.
proof_next_action: In the Shadow repo, locate the shipped false-close audit record and the closure step's auto-close configuration, select the single commitment class with the most Will-reviewed closes in the audit, enable auto-close for that class only, log the widening as an action with the audit receipt and revert condition, run the test suite, and push to main; if the audit record cannot be found in git, record that as a blocker-free finding and do not widen.
